formulas.title: Degree of Unsaturation
formulas.worked: C4H8 (an alkene): DoU = (2×4+2−8)/2 = 2/2 = 1 (matches one double bond or ring)
formulas.note: Each ring or pi bond (double bond) contributes 1; a triple bond contributes 2.

formulas.title: Markovnikov Addition Prediction
formulas.eq: H adds to the carbon with more existing H atoms; X (or OH) adds to the more substituted carbon
formulas.worked: Propene + HBr → 2-bromopropane (Br on the more substituted carbon), not 1-bromopropane
formulas.note: The more stable (more substituted) carbocation forms preferentially, directing where the nucleophile attacks.

formulas.title: Alkene Hydroboration-Oxidation Regiochemistry
formulas.eq: Boron adds to the less hindered carbon; OH ends up there after oxidation (anti-Markovnikov)
formulas.worked: Propene + BH3, then H2O2/OH− → 1-propanol (OH on the terminal carbon)
formulas.note: Concerted syn addition means both new bonds form on the same face of the double bond.

formulas.title: Zaitsev's Rule for Elimination
formulas.eq: Major product = the more substituted (more stable) alkene
formulas.note: Bulky bases like potassium tert-butoxide instead favor the Hofmann (less substituted) product.

formulas.title: SN2 Rate Equation
formulas.worked: Doubling nucleophile concentration doubles the reaction rate in a true SN2 process
formulas.note: Second-order kinetics confirm a single concerted step involving both reactants.

formulas.title: SN1 Rate Equation
formulas.worked: Nucleophile concentration has no effect on rate; only substrate concentration matters
formulas.note: First-order kinetics reflect the slow, rate-determining ionization step forming the carbocation.

formulas.title: Carboxylic Acid pKa Estimation
formulas.eq: Electron-withdrawing groups near -COOH lower pKa (increase acidity)
formulas.worked: Acetic acid pKa ≈ 4.76; trichloroacetic acid (3 Cl atoms) pKa ≈ 0.7
formulas.note: Inductive electron withdrawal stabilizes the conjugate base (carboxylate), increasing acid strength.

formulas.title: Fischer Esterification Equilibrium
formulas.worked: Using excess alcohol or removing water (Dean-Stark trap) shifts equilibrium toward the ester
formulas.note: This is an acid-catalyzed equilibrium reaction, not driven to completion without pushing the equilibrium.

formulas.title: Amide Resonance Stabilization Energy
formulas.eq: Amide resonance contributes roughly 15–20 kcal/mol of rotational barrier around the C-N bond
formulas.worked: This barrier is why amide bonds (including peptide bonds) are essentially planar and rigid
formulas.note: The nitrogen lone pair delocalizes into the carbonyl pi system, giving partial double-bond character to C-N.

formulas.title: Alkyne Acidity (pKa)
formulas.eq: Terminal alkyne C-H pKa ≈ 25 (vs. ~44 for alkane, ~36 for alkene C-H)
formulas.worked: Terminal alkynes can be deprotonated by strong bases like NaNH2 (pKa of NH3 ≈ 38)
formulas.note: Greater s-character in the sp carbon holds electron density closer to the nucleus, stabilizing the resulting anion.

formulas.title: Aromatic Ring Electron Count (Huckel's Rule)
formulas.eq: Aromatic if the ring has 4n+2 pi electrons (n = 0, 1, 2...)
formulas.worked: Benzene has 6 pi electrons: 4(1)+2=6, confirming aromaticity
formulas.note: Ring must also be cyclic, planar, and fully conjugated for Huckel's rule to apply.

formulas.title: Percent Yield Calculation
formulas.worked: Theoretical yield = 10 g, actual yield = 7.5 g → % yield = 7.5/10 × 100 = 75%
formulas.note: Common in lab reports for any synthesis reaction in this course, including esterifications and substitutions.

formulas.title: Molar Mass to Moles Conversion
formulas.worked: 20 g of ethanol (molar mass 46 g/mol) → 20/46 ≈ 0.43 mol
formulas.note: Essential for stoichiometric calculations in any synthesis or titration problem.

cards.q: The six structures (I–VI) shown are all marketed drugs. (a)(i) Identify all of the amine drugs among structures I–VI. (ii) Justify your choice(s). (b) Classify each amine drug you identified as primary, secondary, or tertiary.
cards.a: Amine drugs: I, IV, V and VI. Classification — I: tertiary amine; IV: secondary amine (cyclic/piperidine-type nitrogen); V: primary amine; VI: secondary amine.
cards.e: Structure II is a quaternary ammonium salt (choline/acetylcholine-type): its nitrogen carries four alkyl substituents and a permanent positive charge with no lone pair, so it belongs to a distinct class from amines, not to the amine family itself. Structure III (paracetamol/acetaminophen-type) contains an amide (-NHC(=O)-) linkage, not a free amine — the nitrogen's lone pair is tied up in resonance with the carbonyl, so amides are excluded from the amine family. Structures I, IV, V and VI each carry a genuine amine nitrogen: I has a -N(CH3)2 group attached to a saturated carbon (tertiary amine); IV's nitrogen sits inside a saturated ring bonded to two carbons plus one hydrogen (secondary/cyclic amine); V is a simple primary amine (one C-N bond, two N-H); and VI has its nitrogen bonded to two carbon groups (secondary amine).
